packs.title: Gardens to the Coast
packs.promise: Follow gates, galleries, coast and living collections across four honest outings.

q.s: Make a small composition from pavilion, water and shore.
st: Follow open pedestrian paths to a safe view of Ukimi Pavilion. Use the walking path rather than the jogging or cycling lanes.
Make a three-line drawing or three short written lines: one for the pavilion roof, one for water or reflection, and one for the shore. Use the conditions actually present.
Choose which line should lead the eye and which should remain quiet. Change one line to make that choice clearer.
Name the change and describe how it affected your composition before continuing along the open island and shore paths.

q.s: Find a connection that survives a closer look at the labels.
st: Arrive by the signed Ohori Park visitor entrance before 17:00. Use valid collection admission: standard 200 yen adult, applicable concession or documented free entry. Bring entitlement proof; eligible 65+ residents of Fukuoka, Kitakyushu, Kumamoto or Kagoshima need age and address evidence. Special exhibitions are optional.

Use a pencil for notes and the required lockers or umbrella stands. In open collection rooms, choose two displayed works that share a visible shape, material or compositional idea. No particular artist or work is guaranteed.
Record each displayed title or identifying label and one observation that links them. Read the labels and mark which part of your first interpretation they support or change.
Write a revised two-sentence connection. Keep your own interpretation separate from what the museum states.

q.s: Trace one museum object from evidence to an unanswered question.
st: From Nishijin’s public street exit, take the mapped 1.1 km / 16 min outside-street approach along Sazae-san-dori and Yokatopia-dori to the museum’s west side, beside the General Library. Current works close the southern forecourt: use signed west visitor access, keep out of the closed area and allow 15 min for the unmeasured door approach, admission / lockers. Recheck the operator’s works notice before going. Before 17:00, obtain valid collection admission: standard 200 yen adult or applicable reduced / free entry with required proof. Eligible 65+ four-city residents need age and address evidence.
Use a pencil and required bag or umbrella storage. Find one displayed object whose interpretation describes travel, exchange or a connection beyond the place where it was used.
Collect the displayed object name, the stated connection and one visible detail that helps you understand it. Mark anything you cannot verify as uncertain.
Draw or write an arrow from origin or connection to use, only as supported by the label. Add one question the display leaves unanswered.

packs.title: Hakata in Detail
packs.promise: Read craft, gate patterns, shopfronts and quiet spaces on two connected Hakata afternoons.

q.s: Separate woven structure from a shaped and painted surface.
st: Find the current museum at Hakata Ekimae Park Front 1F, 1-23-2 Hakataekimae. Visit Thursday or Friday between 10:00 and 18:00, entering by 17:30; ordinary exhibition entry is free and workshops are optional.
In the open exhibition, locate an interpreted example of Hakata weaving and one of Hakata doll craft. Collect the displayed names and a label-supported material or process clue for each.
Compare how a repeating thread structure differs from a shaped or painted surface. Record one visible clue from each without touching or pretending to know an unlabelled material.
Write a two-row comparison: craft, stated material or process, and the feature you could actually see. If a label is unclear, mark the uncertainty rather than guessing.

q.s: Read how a covered shopping street explains its businesses.
st: Leave Kushida by an open southwest visitor exit and join Kawabata’s public aisle. Walk north through the arcade toward the route’s selected northern query point; this movement is part of the task.

Collect three different public shopfront messages: one naming a product, one explaining a service, and one helping people find or recognise the business. Copy only what is legible; an unknown language may be recorded as an unknown.
For each, describe one visual feature such as letter scale, colour contrast or placement. Explain how it helps that particular message rather than guessing a shop’s history.
Choose the most useful message for a first-time visitor and explain why. Stop at a safe aisle-side position; purchases, tasting and interviews are optional.

q.s: Make a three-scene story from one public canal-side space.
st: From Canal City’s northeastern public street approach, allow 10–15 min to locate the open 1F canal walk near General Information using the current visitor map. Visit during ordinary daytime opening; no purchase or show ticket is needed.
Choose an open visitor position where a canal curve and more than one built level are visible. Stay on the public walkway, outside water and performance spaces.
Create three drawn frames or three written scenes: arrival, the curve leading your eye, and a changed view from another nearby permitted position. Keep the actual levels and movement plausible.
Give the sequence a short title and explain how the second scene connects the first and last. Return by an open public route to the northeastern street anchor for the Rakusuien walk.
